narrative_purpose: Show the chapter's central mechanism literally: the air leaving the front wing is travelling downward, so the rear wing sitting in it meets tilted flow and works less well.
subject: A side-on cutaway of two wing cross-sections. On the left, one thin cambered wing section pointing right. Behind and slightly below it on the right, a second identical wing section. Between and around them, the airflow is drawn as many long pale flowing lines: entering from the left horizontally, then bending clearly downward as they pass over and behind the first wing section, forming a sinking band of flow that the second wing section sits inside. The flow lines that reach the second section arrive angled downward rather than horizontal.
scene: An abstract dark field with nothing but the two wing sections and the flowing air, like a plate from a naturalist's notebook rather than a landscape.
camera: Flat side elevation, straight on, both wing sections at the same apparent size.
light: The flow lines themselves are the light source: faint self-luminous cool teal, brightest where the air bends downward. The wing sections are dark solid silhouettes.
palette: Deep indigo void, pale cool-teal flowing lines, near-black wing sections, one faint cyan edge highlight on each wing.
style: Painterly hand-worked plate, soft brushed flow lines - not a clean vector schematic and not an infographic.
detail_level: Even and clear throughout; the bend in the flow behind the front wing is the sharpest thing in the frame.
composition: Two wing sections on a gentle descending diagonal left to right, wide plain dark space above and below the flow band framed by deep negative space.
consistency_notes: The single readable idea is that the air behind the first wing is going DOWN and the second wing is inside that descending air. The two wing sections must be identical in shape and size so the difference is clearly the flow and not the wing. Painterly, glowing flow lines on darkness; never a technical vector specimen study.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no labels, no arrowheads, no leader lines, no vector-flat infographic look, no CAD linework, no photographic or 3D render, no cartoon style
